chunks: And what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Safwan from Abdullah from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: A woman received news of her husband's death after a year or thereabouts. He said: If she is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth to her pregnancy; and if she is not pregnant, her waiting period has passed if evidence is established for her that he died on such and such a day; and if she has no evidence, let her observe the waiting period from the day she heard. These two narrations are rare and contradictory to all the other hadiths, and the detail contained in the latter hadith is also contradicted by the preceding narration mentioned from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, because he said: She observes the waiting period from the day the news reaches her, whether evidence is established for her or not. So it is permissible to deviate from the numerous narrations to these two narrations, on the condition that it is permissible that the narrator made a mistake and heard the ruling of the divorced woman and thought it was the ruling of the one whose husband died, because the detail contained in the latter narration regarding the consideration of the establishment of evidence and the completion of the waiting period upon the delivery of the pregnancy and other than that, all of it is considered in it. And upon this interpretation, there is no contradiction between the narrations, and if the distance is close, from one day or two days and what resembles them, it is permissible for her to build upon the day the husband died; and if it is more than that, it is not permissible except that she builds upon the day the news reaches her.

(572) 171 That was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Saif ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman whose husband dies or divorces her while he is absent: If it is a journey of days, she observes the waiting period from the day her husband dies; and if it is from a distance, she observes it from the day the news reaches her, because she must mourn for him.

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: The waiting period of Mut'ah (temporary marriage) is one menstrual period if she is one who menstruates, or forty-five days if she is one who does not menstruate.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman whose husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi analyzes the rarity of reports suggesting the waiting period begins upon hearing news regardless of distance, preferring the majority view that distinguishes between proximity and remoteness to ensure proper mourning (Hudud). He also clarifies the specific duration for temporary marriage (Mut'ah), noting it is three menstrual cycles or 45 days for non-menstruating women, grounded in the principle of obligatory waiting even for absent spouses.
